links.title: Logs
links.tooltip: Logs dashboard, carrying the current time range. Variables are not carried — logs filters on log-group tokens (main/test), not the metric `network` label (mainnet/testnet).

list.name: deployment
list.label: Deployment
list.description: Blue/green colour(s) to include. Multi-select; "All" covers both. Has no effect on the Edge rows — CloudFront and WAF sit in front of both colours.

list.name: network
list.label: Network
list.description: VeChain network(s) to include. Values match the `network` external label emitted by the ADOT sidecar (terraform/api/observability.tf network_label map) — `mainnet`/`testnet`, not the `main`/`test` tokens used in log group names. Applies to the Prometheus panels only; the Edge rows are per-network and fixed.

list.name: filters
list.label: Filters
list.description: Ad-hoc label filters applied to every AMP (Prometheus) panel — uri, status, task_id, collection, command, endpoint, … Replaces the old URI textbox. Does not apply to the CloudWatch Edge rows, which are a different datasource.

panels.title: CloudFront requests (total)
panels.description: AWS/CloudFront Requests (Sum) totalled over the dashboard time range, both distributions collapsed into one figure — the graph beside it keeps them apart. The two series are joined and summed per timestamp in transformations because a stat panel otherwise renders one number per series. Period is left on auto so a range past CloudFront's 15-day 1-minute retention rolls up instead of returning nothing. Edge volume, so it sits above the API row's 'Total requests': cache hits and WAF blocks never reach the origin.

panels.title: Cache hit rate (average)
panels.description: AWS/CloudFront CacheHitRate (Average, %) reduced to one figure: the mean of the per-period averages over the dashboard range, across both distributions. Not a request-weighted hit ratio — CloudFront publishes no hit/miss counts — so a quiet period weighs the same as a busy one, and the spare distribution the same as the primary whenever it serves. Read it beside the graph, not instead of it.

panels.title: CloudFront requests
panels.description: AWS/CloudFront Requests (Sum) across the two distributions fronting indexer.mainnet.vechain.org (E15Q64MS368TL primary, E1LMOFNZTMWN6R spare/replica). Fixed to this network and not affected by the Network or Deployment pickers — CloudFront and WAF are shared across both blue/green colours and are not templated. CloudFront metrics are 1-minute granularity and publish with a few minutes of lag, so this trails the Prometheus panels below.

panels.title: Cache hit rate
panels.description: AWS/CloudFront CacheHitRate (Average, %). Higher = more edge hits, less origin load. The indexer API is largely uncacheable so expect low double digits at best; drops toward zero on cache invalidation or a hot-path change.

panels.title: CloudFront error rate — 4xx / 5xx
panels.description: AWS/CloudFront 4xxErrorRate + 5xxErrorRate (Average, %) — percentage of viewer requests returning 4xx/5xx at the edge. Cross-reference with the API panels in the Errors row: edge errors the origin never saw are WAF blocks or CloudFront-level failures.

panels.title: WAF — allowed vs blocked
panels.description: AWS/WAFV2 AllowedRequests + BlockedRequests (Sum, Rule=ALL). Aggregate across the whole shared-veworld-cloudfront-waf WebACL.

panels.title: WAF — blocked requests by rule
panels.description: AWS/WAFV2 BlockedRequests (Sum) split by Rule. Rule = the CloudWatch metric name from VisibilityConfig.MetricName. Spike hunters: rate-based rule (a customer being throttled), block-ip-set (specific IP blocked), block-get-options-swagger (non-GET/OPTIONS request rejected).

panels.title: WAF — counted requests by rule (dry run)
panels.description: AWS/WAFV2 CountedRequests (Sum). A COUNT rule flags a request and lets it through, so this is what a tighter limit would have caught — nothing here was blocked. "High-rate IP dry run" is waf--custom-AWS-count-high-rate-ip, tripping above high_rate_count_limit requests per IP per 5 min with none of the rate-limit exemptions, so the block-explorer proxy egress would be counted too. While no IP crosses the threshold CloudWatch creates no series for it at all, so it is absent from the legend rather than drawn at zero — "All count-mode rules" is the WebACL-wide aggregate, carried here so the panel still renders and proves the query path is alive; the dry-run rule is a subset of it, which is why the series are not stacked. For the flagged IPs and paths use wafv2 get-sampled-requests — get-rate-based-statement-managed-keys stays empty for a count-only rule, since it lists only keys actually being limited.

panels.title: WAF — blocked requests by rule
panels.description: AWS/WAFV2 BlockedRequests (Sum) split by Rule. Rule = the CloudWatch metric name from VisibilityConfig.MetricName. Testnet does not have the python-user-agent rate-limit rule that mainnet does.

panels.title: Indexers by sync status
panels.description: count by (status) of indexers where indexer_sync_status == 1. Deduped across task_id — deployment/network are kept in the inner max so a shared indexer_name across networks isn't collapsed — and constrained to the last 45s so post-deploy stale series drop out before the default 5m lookback.

targets.expr: count by (status) (max by (indexer_name, status, deployment, network) (last_over_time(indexer_sync_status{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", indexer_name=~"$indexer_name", service="indexer"}[45s])) == 1)

panels.title: Sync gap — blocks behind Thor best
panels.description: max(thor_best) − max(indexer_current) per indexer, clamped to ≥ 0 and forced to 0 when the indexer reports FULLY_SYNCED (raw block-number diff can drift 1–3 blocks from sampling timing even when caught up). Bars sorted by gap desc, indexer name asc as tiebreaker; > 100 orange, > 500 red.

targets.expr: clamp_min((max by (deployment, network) (thor_best_block_number{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", service="indexer"}) - on(deployment, network) group_right() max by (deployment, network, indexer_name) (indexer_current_block{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", indexer_name=~"$indexer_name", service="indexer"})) * on(deployment, network, indexer_name) group_left() (1 - max by (deployment, network, indexer_name) (indexer_sync_status{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", indexer_name=~"$indexer_name", status="FULLY_SYNCED", service="indexer"})), 0)

panels.title: Blocks / sec
panels.description: rate(indexer_blocks_processed_total[1m]) per indexer.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (indexer_name, le) (rate(processor_duration_seconds_bucket{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", indexer_name=~"$indexer_name"}[5m])))

panels.title: Total requests
panels.description: Every request the API served over the dashboard time range — the denominator the two topk panels beside it hide. `increase()` is summed per step rather than taken over `$__range` in one shot so the sparkline has a shape; the step is floored at 1m because the sidecar scrapes at 15s and a shorter window can hold too few samples for `increase()` to return anything. Counts what reached the API, so it sits below the Edge row's 'CloudFront requests': cache hits and WAF blocks never arrive here.

panels.title: Top URIs by total origin time
panels.description: topk(15) of sum by (uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_sum[$__range])) — total seconds of server time each endpoint consumed over the dashboard time range, i.e. request count × mean latency. This is the panel to act on: an endpoint can be the busiest by count and cost almost nothing here (the usual shape for cheap per-user lookups), while a low-volume endpoint with a slow query can dominate. Pair with 'API — avg latency by URI' to see which of the two factors drives a bar.

panels.title: Top URIs by total requests
panels.description: topk(15) of sum by (uri) (increase(http_server_requests_seconds_count[$__range])) — absolute request counts over the dashboard time range, not a rate, so bursty and steady traffic are comparable. Ranks by count, not by cost: a path can top this panel and still be near-free, so check 'Top URIs by total origin time' before acting on a bar here. `/**` is Spring's catch-all pattern: every request whose path matched no controller mapping, i.e. all unmatched-path 404s aggregated into one bar. The `uri` label is the matched Spring pattern with the query string stripped, so every parameter shape of one endpoint shares a bar. Full paths and query strings come from the ALB access logs in S3 (prod-{blue,green}-veworld-{main,test}-api-ecs-lb-bucket, prefix veworld-lb/). The mainnet WAF log group logs BLOCKed requests only (logging_filter_block_only), so it is not a traffic census; testnet's logs everything.

panels.title: API — avg latency by URI
panels.description: rate(sum) / rate(count). Real p95 needs percentile histograms enabled server-side (management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram.http.server.requests=true).

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_sum{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", service="api"}[5m])) / sum by (uri) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", service="api"}[5m])))

panels.title: Requests by X-Project-Id
panels.description: sum by (project) of api_requests_by_project_total increases over the dashboard time range. `unknown` = header missing; `other` = header set but not on the KNOWN_PROJECT_IDS whitelist (raw value logged); the rest are known callers.

panels.title: Top URIs by rate
panels.description: topk(10) of request rate by uri, ranked per timestamp — a URI that goes quiet drops out of the top 10, so its line breaks into a gap rather than sitting at zero. Legend shows Max/Last only: Mean would average the bursts and ignore the gaps, which reads ~20x too high on spiky series like `/**`. For volume use 'Top URIs by total requests'. Narrow to a single endpoint with the Filters bar at the top (uri = …).

targets.expr: sum by (uri, status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", service="api", outcome="SERVER_ERROR"}[5m]))
sum by (uri, status) (rate(http_server_requests_seconds_count{deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network", service="api", outcome="CLIENT_ERROR"}[5m]))

panels.title: API tasks running against desired
panels.description: A gap that outlasts a rolling deploy is a stuck deploy or a placement failure; the `*-api-tasks-below-desired` alarm fires on the same two metrics. API services only: the indexers deploy at deployment_minimum_healthy_percent = 0, so a rolling replacement legitimately sits at zero running tasks for minutes and a gap there says nothing. Service-level counts come from ECS itself, so a dead task reads as a drop to zero — the ADOT per-task series behind the two panels below just go absent instead. CloudWatch dimensions cannot be templated, so both colours and both networks are hardcoded here and neither picker applies.

panels.title: CPU utilised — per task
panels.description: ecs_task_cpu_utilized / ecs_task_cpu_reserved × 100 for indexer + api. Dashed line = 80%.

panels.title: Memory utilised — per task
panels.description: ecs_task_memory_utilized / ecs_task_memory_reserved × 100 for indexer + api. Dashed line = 80%.

panels.title: Pool size vs checked-out
panels.description: mongodb_driver_pool_size vs mongodb_driver_pool_checkedout. Sustained checkedout ≈ size means the pool is saturated — either bump the pool or fix a slow query.

panels.title: Wait-queue depth
panels.description: mongodb_driver_pool_waitqueuesize — connections waiting for a pool slot. Anything > 0 sustained means the pool is under-sized for the workload.

panels.title: Command rate by status
panels.description: rate(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_count[5m]) by status. FAILED > 0 means Mongo is rejecting commands (auth, write conflict, timeout, …).

panels.title: Command rate — top 10 by command
panels.description: topk(10, rate by command) — expect insert/update/find to dominate on the indexer.

panels.title: Avg command latency by command
panels.description: rate(sum)/rate(count) by command — proxy for average latency per command type. Real p95 needs management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram.mongodb.driver.commands=true.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (command) (rate(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_sum{service="indexer", deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network"}[5m])) / sum by (command) (rate(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_count{service="indexer", deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network"}[5m])))

panels.title: Command rate — top 10 by collection
panels.description: topk(10, rate by collection) — which collections are being hit hardest.

panels.title: Slowest commands — max latency
panels.description: max over 5m of mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_max by (command, collection). Spike hunter — surfaces single slow calls the avg smooths away.

targets.expr: topk(10, max by (command, collection) (max_over_time(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_max{service="indexer", deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network"}[5m])))

panels.title: Pool size vs checked-out
panels.description: mongodb_driver_pool_size vs mongodb_driver_pool_checkedout. Sustained checkedout ≈ size means the pool is saturated — either bump the pool or fix a slow query.

panels.title: Wait-queue depth
panels.description: mongodb_driver_pool_waitqueuesize — API requests waiting for a pool slot. Anything > 0 sustained will surface as user-visible latency.

panels.title: Command rate by status
panels.description: rate(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_count[5m]) by status. FAILED > 0 means Mongo is rejecting API requests before they reach the response path.

panels.title: Command rate — top 10 by command
panels.description: topk(10, rate by command) — expect find/aggregate to dominate on the API.

panels.title: Avg command latency by command
panels.description: rate(sum)/rate(count) by command — proxy for average latency per command type. Real p95 needs management.metrics.distribution.percentiles-histogram.mongodb.driver.commands=true.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (command) (rate(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_sum{service="api", deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network"}[5m])) / sum by (command) (rate(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_count{service="api", deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network"}[5m])))

panels.title: Command rate — top 10 by collection
panels.description: topk(10, rate by collection) — which collections API traffic hits hardest; cross-reference with the Top URIs panel above.

panels.title: Slowest commands — max latency
panels.description: max over 5m of mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_max by (command, collection). Spike hunter — surfaces single slow queries the avg smooths away.

targets.expr: topk(10, max by (command, collection) (max_over_time(mongodb_driver_commands_seconds_max{service="api", deployment=~"$deployment", network=~"$network"}[5m])))

panels.title: WAF request detail · Mainnet — Logs Insights, runs only while expanded
Flagged traffic over the range
panels.description: The denominator for the two tables below, from the WAF log group in us-east-1 (CLOUDFRONT-scope ACLs log there, not eu-west-1). This group carries BLOCKed requests only — logging_filter_block_only is on for mainnet — so it is a rejection census, not a traffic one; total edge volume is 'CloudFront requests' in the Edge · Mainnet row. Where clients and paths run to thousands, the top 20 rows below are the head of a long tail rather than its bulk.

targets.expression:
filter terminatingRuleId != "Default_Action" or ispresent(nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId)
| stats count(*) as flagged, count_distinct(httpRequest.clientIp) as clients, count_distinct(httpRequest.uri) as paths

panels.title: Flagged clients
panels.description: Who tripped a rule, by source IP. `flagged` counts that client's matched requests, never its whole traffic. `rule` is the WebACL rule name, the same vocabulary as the Rule dimension in 'WAF — blocked requests by rule'. `action` reads BLOCK throughout while no rule runs in Count mode (the managed groups use override_action none); ALLOW would mean a count-mode dry run that was still served. A cloud scraper spreads itself over a range, so one actor arrives here as many small rows — the totals above are its real size.

targets.expression:
fields httpRequest.clientIp as clientIp, httpRequest.country as country, httpRequest.uri as path, coalesce(nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId, terminatingRuleId, labels.0.name) as rule
| filter terminatingRuleId != "Default_Action" or ispresent(nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId)
| stats count(*) as flagged, count_distinct(path) as paths, count_distinct(rule) as rules by clientIp, country, action
| sort flagged desc
| limit 20

panels.title: Flagged paths
panels.description: What those requests asked for. Indexer API routes mean real callers behind a flagged IP range; probe paths — wp-login, .env, phpmyadmin — mean the rule is earning its place. `clients` is how many distinct sources asked for that path. Paths are full request URIs, so one endpoint spreads across many rows here where 'Top URIs by total requests' collapses it into one Spring pattern.

targets.expression:
fields httpRequest.uri as path, httpRequest.httpMethod as method, httpRequest.clientIp as clientIp, coalesce(nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId, terminatingRuleId, labels.0.name) as rule
| filter terminatingRuleId != "Default_Action" or ispresent(nonTerminatingMatchingRules.0.ruleId)
| stats count(*) as flagged, count_distinct(clientIp) as clients by path, method, rule
| sort flagged desc
| limit 20
